analysis.title: Upstart Holdings (UPST): 3Q26 First Take: Beat and lower likely to weigh on shares
key_insights: GS calls the UPST 3Q26 print disappointing: a solid quarterly beat on much higher than expected contribution margins, but a lower FY26 outlook implies a much worse than expected 4Q exit run-rate.
Shares were very weak heading into the print, which GS expects to muddle the post-earnings reaction. GS says the lower 4Q outlook is likely to weigh on sentiment.

The Upstart Macro Index (UMI) rose to 1.53, its highest since November 2025. GS reads this as a modest deterioration in consumer credit conditions and modestly higher default rates versus historical averages. It will likely add to concerns about a volume slowdown.
Monthly originations were $1,249.2mn in October. Origination growth was 21% y/y in October, down from 44% in September.
Contribution margins on secured lending products (auto, HELOC) were solidly positive in the quarter, which GS flags as a positive.

FY26 guidance: revenue of about $1.35bn (consensus $1.42bn, 4.9% below), revenue from fees $1.32bn (in line with consensus $1.323bn), adjusted EBITDA about $260mn at a 19% margin (consensus $290mn, 10.5% below), net interest income $30mn (consensus $97mn).

Implied 4Q26 guide: revenue $307mn vs consensus $383mn (19.9% below), adjusted EBITDA $53mn vs consensus $92mn (41.9% below), revenue from fees $331mn vs consensus $358mn, net interest income of -$24mn vs consensus +$25mn.

GS questions for the call: what is driving the fall in EBITDA, updated opex expectations exiting the year and into next year, and the outlook for further contribution margin improvement on secured products.
Some of the guide-down could be attributed to the higher UMI, but GS wants more color on what is driving the sequential fall-off in volumes (see October volume deceleration) and EBITDA.
GS rates UPST Neutral with a 12-month price target of $28 (11x multiple on Q5-Q8 adjusted EBITDA-SBC estimates), against a $21.31 close on 2 Nov 2026, or 31.4% upside. Market cap is $2.1bn.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral with a $28 target after a 3Q26 beat on contribution margin, but flags a lower FY26 outlook and an implied 4Q26 that is well below consensus as likely to weigh on shares.

earnings_insights: UPST 3Q26 (reported 11/3 before the open): net revenue from fees $364mn vs Visible Alpha consensus $342mn (7% ahead), vs GS est $329mn.
3Q26 transaction volume was $4.12bn vs ~$4.14bn consensus (in line), with take rate about 8.8% vs 8.2% consensus.
3Q26 contribution profit was $218mn (60% margin) vs $190mn (56%) consensus.
3Q26 adjusted EBITDA was $89mn (24% margin) vs consensus $81.5mn (22%) and GS est $79.1mn.

3Q26 EPS was $0.23 per the GS first-take text vs consensus $0.22, while the GS Exhibit 1 shows reported EPS of $0.33 vs GS est $0.19 and consensus $0.22. GS notes the figures may not reconcile due to converts.
3Q26 fixed operating expenses were 6% above consensus per the text, while Exhibit 1 shows $188mn vs consensus $191mn.
3Q26 net interest income was $6.5mn vs consensus $23.6mn and $18.6mn a year earlier.
Segment volumes in 3Q26: personal $3,531mn, auto $411mn (19% below GS est), HELOC $176mn.
FY26 guidance (given with results): revenue about $1.35bn, revenue from fees $1.32bn, adjusted EBITDA about $260mn (19% margin). GS 12/26E EPS is $0.60 and its 12/26E quarterly EPS is $0.32.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest since November 2025. GS reads it as modestly worse consumer credit conditions and modestly higher default rates than historical averages. The text also refers to a sequential increase in November.

risk_factors: Lower FY26 outlook implies a much worse than expected 4Q exit run-rate (revenue $307mn and adjusted EBITDA $53mn vs consensus $383mn and $92mn).
Volume slowdown: October origination growth slowed to 21% y/y from 44% in September, and UMI rose to 1.53.
Net interest income guided to $30mn for FY26 vs $97mn consensus, implying negative net interest income in 4Q26.
GS lists upside/downside risks to the price target as a faster or slower recovery, adoption of domestic payments offerings, and a better or worse competitive landscape.
vol_and_positioning: Shares were very weak heading into the print (close of $21.31 on 2 Nov, vs $23.83 on 13 Oct), which GS says should muddle the post-earnings reaction.

tension_points.bull_case: Contribution margin beat on much higher than expected CP margins, and secured lending contribution margins were solidly positive. Some of the guide-down can be attributed to the higher UMI.
tension_points.bear_case: The lower FY26 outlook implies 4Q26 revenue of $307mn vs $383mn consensus and EBITDA of $53mn vs $92mn. October origination growth slowed to 21% y/y from 44%, and UMI rose to 1.53.

theme_stances.key_argument: The lower 4Q outlook is likely to weigh on sentiment despite the quarterly beat.
theme_stances.evidence: lower outlook in the 4th quarter is likely to weigh on sentiment
